title: Eventual surjectivity of restriction of projective twists
statement:
Let k be a field, let c:Y -> P^N_k be a closed immersion, and let w:Z -> Y be a
closed immersion whose image is finite. For all sufficiently large natural numbers n,
the canonical map pullbackGamma(w,O_Y(n)) from global sections on Y to global sections
of w^*O_Y(n) on Z is surjective. O_Y(n) and the section maps use
[def-zl-prescribed-point-system-data, def-pc-module-pullback].

proof.text: The proper finite-type scheme Y is locally Noetherian. The quasi-coherent ideal ker(w) is of finite presentation. Apply Serre vanishing for a closed projective embedding to its ordinary projective twists, and transport by the comparison from ordinary to tensor pullback.

For an invertible module P the ideal multiplication map mu:ker(w) tensor P -> P is mono. The closed-immersion unit kernel theorem makes 0 -> image(mu) -> P -> w_* w^*P -> 0 short exact. Identify image(mu) with its source. H^1 of that source vanishes for the degrees above the Serre bound. The cohomology exact sequence then makes the unit surjective on global sections.

Uniqueness of left adjoints compares the chosen tensor-pullback adjunction with ordinary pullback, carrying the unit to pullbackGamma. The comparison on its pushforward is an isomorphism and is surjective on sections, so the composite map is surjective. Use toNat of the integral Serre bound for the requested natural-number bound.

mathlib_searches.query: High twists of a sheaf on a projective scheme restrict surjectively to global sections on a closed subscheme by Serre vanishing
mathlib_searches.results: IsClosedImmersion.of_surjective_of_isAffine and subschemeι_app_surjective concern affine structure sheaves, not high invertible twists.

mathlib_searches.query: Restriction of global sections to a closed subscheme is surjective after a sufficiently high projective twist
mathlib_searches.results: ProjIsoSpecTopComponent.toSpec_surjective and subschemeι_app_surjective do not give eventual global restriction for modules.
No projective-twist restriction theorem in Mathlib; results include unrelated analytic restrictions and Serre number-theory names.

theorem exists_eventual_projectiveTwist_restriction_surjective
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {N : ℕ} {Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (c : Y ⟶ ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin (N + 1)); Spec (.of k))) [IsClosedImmersion c]
    (w : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion w] (hw : (Set.range w).Finite) :
    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n →
      Function.Surjective (pullbackΓ w (prescribedPointTwist c n))
